extracted.intended_audience: researchers and prospective authors in combinatorial mathematics (potential manuscript submitters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level criteria for submitting research manuscripts to the Annals of Combinatorics, including scope, topical emphasis, expectations of novelty/impact, and procedural notes such as special-issue submission and processing speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Annals of Combinatorics is a journal focused on publishing exceptional contributions to combinatorial mathematics in all its aspects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should submit work that lies within combinatorial mathematics broadly; the journal's stated mission is to cover the full breadth of combinatorics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical emphasis
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasis on algebraic and analytic combinatorics, and areas of graph and matroid theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions in these emphasized subfields are especially aligned with the journal's interests; for special collections (e.g., in memory of Andreas Dress) authors should ensure topical alignment with the call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of novelty and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Presents new developments in the field that show promise of eventual mathematical breakthroughs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should contain original results or developments whose significance suggests potential for important future impact; incremental or purely expository work is less likely to meet this bar.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality standard — 'exceptional contributions'
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is focused on publishing exceptional contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should meet a high quality threshold in terms of correctness, depth, clarity, and significance appropriate for a research journal aiming to publish leading work in combinatorics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special issues / topical collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal issues Calls for Papers for special Topical Collections (example: 'In Memory of Andreas Dress: Mathematical and Combinatorial Approaches...'). Status and deadlines (e.g., 'Open for submissions', 'Submission deadline 15 July 2026') are specified for each call.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit to a special issue authors should select the Special Issue during submission and follow the submission guidelines; check the call details (scope, deadlines, any additional requirements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission procedural expectation — follow submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are directed to 'submit your manuscript' and to 'see the submission guidelines to read more details'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts must follow the journal's submission guidelines (formatting, cover letter, declarations, etc.) — authors should consult the linked submission guidelines for specific requirements before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing speed metric
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal emphasizes efficient and speedy processing of submitted manuscripts; authors can expect a relatively short median time to first decision, though actual times may vary by submission and review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal impact and discoverability indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Impact Factor 0.7 (2024); 5-year Journal Impact Factor 0.8 (2024); indexed/abstracted in numerous services (e.g., SCOPUS, Science Citation Index Expanded, zbMATH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These metrics and indexing listings indicate reach and discoverability; authors may consider them when deciding where to submit, but they do not replace the journal's thematic and quality expectations.
